answer: The press house keeps a pruning register, and every row of vines is entered there once its canes are cut and the cuttings weighed. A velvet row claimed as pruned is struck from the book, because the register shows which hands cut each cane, and a row no pruner touched still stands uncut. Faking one season means hiring a crew, cutting nine hundred vines and paying 12,400 in wages, while the echo stamp on the register page is pressed in wax, so a second claim on the same row is caught at once, and the jetty entry stays open until the master signs it.
